hero.eyebrow: FREE · OPEN SOURCE · RUNS ON YOUR HARDWARE
hero.title:
Your GPU already does this.
Stop paying monthly for it.
hero.subtitle: OPNduck is a media processing suite for AI upscaling, frame interpolation, downloading, and format conversion — all running locally, on the machine you already own. Nothing uploaded, nothing metered, nothing rented back to you.

gallery.title: Home workspace
gallery.caption: Tool cards are generated from installed features and plugins — install one and a card appears here automatically.

gallery.title: Settings
gallery.caption: Global configuration: three main themes plus 24 Omarchy palettes, menu-icon style, motion and density, keybinds, job queue, GPU performance, notifications and more.

shipped: Video downloader (yt-dlp) with playlists, subtitles, login cookies and subscriptions
Converter for media, images and documents
AI upscaler (image + video) and frame interpolation
Subtitles with Whisper, AI audio (vocal removal, voice isolation)
Job queue, watch folder, notifications and tray
Faster GPU engine: PyTorch streaming + NVENC
MCP server so AI apps can drive OPNduck
Library with search, filters, groups, export and import
Themes: Blarange, Monochrome, Osaka Jade + 24 Omarchy palettes
Recipes: chain tools into one-click pipelines
Send to OPNduck: links from your phone, browser or another PC
Colour Grade, Background Remover, Beat Finder, Dubbing (Beta)
AI: chat, spoken-word search, summaries, chapters, thumbnail picker, a local model of its own
OPNduck Server and Android app: run jobs on another machine
Assistant: internet access, settings and theme changes, activity icons

blog.title: v0.6.1 Beta — a quick follow-up
blog.author: Ducky
blog.excerpt: The assistant can use the internet and change settings, shows what it is doing, and the local model no longer runs out of memory. Settings are tidier and Home is more compact. Still a Beta: expect bugs.
blog.body:
A quick follow-up to v0.6.0, still a very large Beta: expect bugs and report them.
NEW
The assistant can use the internet (off by default): web search and reading pages, with Wikipedia, Brave Search, your own SearXNG server or DuckDuckGo. It never opens addresses on your computer or home network.
The assistant can change settings and the theme when you ask ("something green", "reduce motion"). You confirm each change with a card.
The assistant shows what it is doing with an animated icon: waking up, thinking, looking something up, preparing a plan, writing.
Settings are sorted into 8 categories. Home is more compact while a tool is open. Recipes and Chat have their own menu icon animations.
FIXED
Chat no longer says "Context size has been exceeded" with OPNduck's own model.
The local AI engine now stops when you eject it or quit OPNduck, and a leftover one is stopped before a new one loads.
The assistant knows where OPNduck's own settings are and says when internet access is off.
Downloads and notes: github.com/Sight8218/OPNduck/releases

blog.title: v0.6.0 Beta — the biggest update yet
blog.author: Ducky
blog.excerpt: The biggest update yet, and possibly ever: recipes, send-to-OPNduck, AI chat and tools, colour grading, background removal, dubbing, a server, an Android app and a macOS beta. It might be super buggy.
blog.body:
This is the biggest update OPNduck has had, and possibly will ever have, and it might be super buggy. Please report what breaks.
Colour Grade: fixes washed-out, dark or tinted footage by itself (it measures the picture and says why it changed each setting), six built-in looks (warm film, teal and orange, bleach bypass, rich black and white, vintage fade, cool night), your own .cube LUTs, matching the look of a reference picture, an AI "make it look like..." option, and sliders with a live before/after. HDR is tone-mapped first.
Background Remover: cuts a person or object out of a picture or video with no green screen. Put behind it: transparent (PNG, WebM or ProRes with alpha), a colour, a blurred copy or another picture. One-frame preview. Add-on download about 150 MB.
Dubbing (Beta): makes a video speak English, Swedish, German, French, Spanish or Italian, all locally: the voice is split from the music, written down (Whisper), translated (Argos), spoken by a free Piper voice and fitted into the timing; the picture is not re-encoded. The dub is a first audio track (original kept as second) or replaces the audio. No voice cloning.
Beat Finder: BPM, beat times and musical key (DJ notation), waveform with a line on every beat, tap tempo, writes the tags, and cuts a set of clips to the beat of a song.
Restore: deinterlace (only when really interlaced), denoise, stabilize and colour fixes for old or shaky footage, with a before/after slider; can chain into upscale and interpolation.
Jump Cut: removes the silences from talking videos and podcasts, with loudness normalizing.
Compress: land just under a size (20 MB for Discord, 16 MB for WhatsApp, 25 MB for email).
GIF & Stickers: GIF, animated WebP, Telegram video stickers and Discord stickers.
Music Tagger: artist, title, album, year, track and cover art for MP3, FLAC, M4A, Ogg and Opus, with a Fix tags button in the Library and optional automatic tagging of new downloads.
Recipes: chain tools into one saved flow (for example download as MP3, then tag it; or upscale, then smooth the motion). Also in the terminal app, in the watch folder and through MCP.
Auto settings: an Auto button on the upscalers, interpolation, subtitles and compress that looks at your file and picks settings.
AI (OFF BY DEFAULT)
AI runtime (Settings > AI): Ollama or LM Studio on this computer, another computer over Tailscale, or a cloud API with your own key (OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini). Keys are kept in the system keyring. Optional monthly token limit.
OPNduck's own model: downloads a small open model (Ministral 3 3B, sees pictures; or Qwen3 1.7B) and the llama.cpp engine, both checked against published checksums, loads when needed and ejects when idle (also from the tray).
Chat page and a terminal Ask screen: streaming answers; it proposes jobs as cards and only runs them when you press Run, and only on files you picked.
Spoken words: transcripts of your videos made on your computer, searchable from the Library (a hit opens the trimmer at that moment), plus summaries, chapters (written into a copy without re-encoding), questions about a video, and a thumbnail picker.
Why did this fail? plain-language reasons for the errors people actually hit; Tidy name for downloads; Colour Grade AI looks.
Share the AI model with your paired devices in the OpenAI format (never a cloud key). npm run ai:eval checks the prompts against a model.
SEND TO OPNDUCK, SERVER AND PHONE
Send to OPNduck: links from your phone, browser or another PC land in OPNduck (off by default) through an opnduck:// link, a direct connection (this computer, Tailscale or home network), or an end-to-end encrypted ntfy relay. A Chrome/Firefox extension and a phone web page are included. It only ever carries a link.
OPNduck Server: the engine without a window for a home server, NAS or container (opnduck-server, Docker images, compose files for NVIDIA, AMD/Intel and Tailscale). Settings > Servers adds one by pair link; every tool card gets a Run on menu, and jobs on a server show up in your queue and Library.
Android companion (first version): pair by QR code, send links (also from any app's Share menu), watch the queue, download results.
Per-device sharing: a phone or extension only sees and manages the jobs it started. Only a device paired with opnduck-server pair --admin sees everything.
PLATFORMS, SYSTEM AND PLUGINS
macOS (Beta): Apple silicon build, smoke-tested on a Mac in CI. Not notarized, so the first launch needs "Open Anyway" (see docs/MACOS.md). Homebrew tools are found even from the Dock; VideoToolbox and Metal are used.
Smart scheduling: only start heavy jobs in a time window, hold them on battery, pause the GPU job when it gets hot.
Plugin system (beta): plugins can add cards and background scripts, each behind permissions you approve; a Plugins page and an index of community plugins.
First-launch setup wizard, community files (code of conduct, contributing, security policy, issue forms).
FIXED
A round of code-audit fixes: remote jobs wrongly refused, upload bookkeeping, look-alike private hostnames, AI engine downloads now need a published checksum, jobs from another device are never forwarded to a third, the ntfy relay reconnects after silence, resumed downloads can't corrupt files, chats save to the right chat, Grade and Dubbing cope with odd audio and subtitle tracks.
The full list is in CHANGELOG.md.
The Windows builds were made from Linux and have not been tried on real Windows. macOS and Android are unsigned. Downloads and notes: github.com/Sight8218/OPNduck/releases

blog.title: v0.5.3 Beta — OPNduck in your terminal
blog.author: Ducky
blog.excerpt: A terminal version of OPNduck (also on npm) that uses about 100 MB instead of about 680 MB, plus a first-launch setup wizard that lets you pick what to install.
blog.body:
New: OPNduck TUI. All eight tools in a terminal with forms, path completion, live progress, a queue, library, settings and all the themes. It shares settings and history with the desktop app. Install with npm i -g opnduck-tui (needs Node.js 20 or newer) or unpack the tarball from the release.
New: a setup wizard on first launch (and in Settings, System) that lists the downloader, the fast video engine, Audio AI and Subtitles with their sizes and installs what you tick.
Under the hood the job code moved into Electron-free modules; the desktop app behaves the same.
The Tauri migration is still postponed: WebKitGTK stutters and crashes on NVIDIA + Wayland, so OPNduck stays on Electron for now.

blog.title: v0.5.2 Beta — a calmer, pixel-style look
blog.author: Ducky
blog.excerpt: Home is a compact grid of tool tiles, there is a themed startup screen, a pixel wordmark, sharper corners, calmer colours and readable text in every theme.
blog.body:
Home now shows a small tile for each tool and opens only the one you pick, so the page is no longer crowded.
A new startup screen with a bobbing duck follows the theme you chose. The wordmark and a faint scatter of pixels give the app a blocky pixel look.
Colours are calmer (orange only for actions and the active item), corners are sharper, and dim text and icons are now readable in every Omarchy palette.
Engine checks are remembered between launches, so cards load faster, and there are more developer tools.
The Tauri migration is still postponed: WebKitGTK stutters and crashes on NVIDIA + Wayland, so OPNduck stays on Electron for now.

blog.title: v0.5.1 Beta — AI apps can drive OPNduck
blog.author: Ducky
blog.excerpt: An optional local MCP server lets Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and other AI apps start and watch OPNduck jobs. Plus animated menu icons and a few things to find.
blog.body:
A new optional MCP server (off by default, Settings → System) lets any MCP-capable AI app start downloads, conversions, upscales, trims and subtitles, watch progress and cancel jobs. It only listens on your own computer, needs a private token, and saves only to your download folder.
The menu icons now animate: the gear spins, the plug sparks, the books get pulled out, the house hops.
There is also something hiding for the curious.

blog.title: v0.5.0 Beta — the performance update
blog.author: Ducky
blog.excerpt: A faster GPU video engine (PyTorch streaming + NVENC), a trimmer with a visual editor, queue controls, watch folder, notifications, live logs on every card, Electron 45 and 24 new Omarchy palettes.
blog.body:
Video upscaling can now stream frames straight through the GPU and encode with NVENC: 1.4x to 3.6x faster end to end in my tests, depending on scale.
Long videos are processed in chunks so temp disk use stays small.
New: trimmer with a visual editor, pause/resume queue, parallel job limits, watch folder, finish notifications and tray mode, live logs on every card and a progress bar that only moves forward.
The Tauri migration is postponed: WebKitGTK stutters and crashes on NVIDIA + Wayland, so OPNduck stays on Electron for now.
